Akwa Ibom State Governor, Umo Eno, has urged indigenes of the state living in Lagos and other parts of the country to unite behind his administration’s development agenda, saying their collective support is important to the state’s progress. According to a statement seen by The PUNCH, the governor made the appeal at the Akwa Ibom Interdenominational Prayer Rally in Lagos, where he was represented by the state’s Liaison Officer in Lagos, Anthony Isonguyo. Eno said the liaison office was intended to strengthen the relationship between the state government and Akwa Ibom indigenes living outside the state, particularly by bringing them together to contribute to its development. Speaking on behalf of the governor, Isonguyo said uniting Akwa Ibom residents in Lagos had been his principal assignment since assuming office. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. And that is the mandate I was given when I was appointed the liaison officer of Akwa Ibom in Lagos. Go to Lagos and unite all Akwa Ibom people. So my project in Lagos is Akwa Ibom United,” he said. He said he was encouraged that speakers at the rally repeatedly emphasised unity, arguing that cooperation among indigenes outside the state would strengthen their capacity to support its development. The governor also described prayer as a central pillar of his administration, saying spiritual guidance remained important to its activities. “The backbone of the government in Akwa Ibom is prayers. Aside from the fact that the governor is an ordained man of God, whatever we do, our background is prayers,” he said. Eno described the gathering as timely and urged Akwa Ibom indigenes in Lagos and the diaspora to support projects being undertaken by his administration, including the state airport and Arise Palm Resort. The rally, organised under the theme ‘Arise & Shine’, was convened by the Apostolic Overseer of Sure Word Assembly Global, Dennis Inyang. Inyang said the initiative was inspired by a spiritual prompting to bring Akwa Ibom people together to pray for the state and strengthen their bonds, particularly among those living outside its borders. He urged the governor to remain focused on delivering development, expressing the hope that a second term would provide an opportunity for greater achievements if Eno secured re-election. “I believe that we are at a very critical point in the history of our state. We will either move forward or go backwards. And when we are at that point, we need God to help us navigate through whatever challenges there may be,” Inyang said. The chairman of the planning committee, Sunny Obot, called on Akwa Ibom indigenes to pray for peaceful elections in 2027, warning political stakeholders against actions that could trigger violence. Obot, who described the governor’s performance as encouraging, said expectations had risen about what his administration could accomplish in the coming years. The gathering attracted Akwa Ibom indigenes from the state’s 31 local government areas and other participants. Ayoola Babalola
